featured.title: India's First Private Orbital Rocket Is Ready to Fly. The Launch Window Opens in a Week.
featured.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 — seven stories tall, carbon composite, 3D-printed engines — will attempt to reach orbit from Sriharikota as early as July 12. A $1 billion valuation says the market believes it can.
featured.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota, India's first private space launch in 2022
featured.nri_angle: For Indian aerospace engineers at SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Boeing, Skyroot represents a credible private space company in India — a career path and investment opportunity that did not exist five years ago.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian-Made Gasoline Is Reaching Russia Through Traders. New Delhi Says It Has Nothing to Do With It.
news.excerpt: As Ukrainian drone strikes cripple a third of Russia's refining capacity, fuel from Nayara Energy — 49% owned by Rosneft — is sailing north via intermediaries. India's oil minister insists no Indian company is selling directly. The distinction may not hold for long.
news.nri_angle: India-Russia fuel trade complicates the India-US trade deal that directly affects five million Indian Americans and Indian exporters.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Washington Says a Historic India-US Trade Deal Is 'Very Very Close.' India Says Not Until It Gets Better Terms Than Pakistan.
news.excerpt: At the USISPF summit in Washington, American officials project imminent success on a $500 billion trade target. But India's Commerce Minister has drawn an unmovable red line: no deal unless Indian tariffs fall below Pakistan's. The gap is 2.5 percentage points — and it could take months to close.
news.image_caption: Wikipedia portrait of Vinay Mohan Kwatra
news.nri_angle: The India-US trade deal directly affects five million Indian Americans, Indian IT firms operating in the US, and the regulatory environment for Global Capability Centres.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The July Visa Bulletin Just Shut the Door on India's EB-2 Green Cards. It Will Not Reopen Until October.
news.excerpt: EB-2 India declared unavailable for the rest of FY2026, EB-1 retrogressed by two months, and EB-5 unreserved also shut — the worst mid-year bulletin for Indian professionals in years.
news.image_caption: The U.S. State Department building in Washington, D.C. — the July 2026 Visa Bulletin has retrogressed EB-2 India to unavailable (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US face frozen green card applications until October, with EB-2 declared unavailable and EB-1 retrogressing — the worst mid-year bulletin in years.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Wants Access to Anthropic's Most Powerful AI. Washington Is Listening — Carefully.
news.excerpt: New Delhi is in talks to use Anthropic's Project Glasswing to stress-test India's critical digital infrastructure, as both countries navigate the geopolitics of frontier AI.
news.image_caption: Frontier AI models are at the heart of US-India technology negotiations (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI professionals work at the heart of America's frontier AI companies; the US-India partnership on model access will determine how freely their expertise flows between both ecosystems.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Trump Accounts Just Went Live. For Indian-American Families, the Math Is Extraordinarily Good.
news.excerpt: The government's new $1,000 seed investment program launched on July 4. With Indian Americans among the highest-earning groups in the U.S., their families are uniquely positioned to maximize it — but only if they act fast.
news.image_caption: The U.S. Treasury Department building in Washington, D.C., which oversees the new Trump Accounts program
news.nri_angle: Indian-American families — among the highest-earning in the U.S. — are uniquely positioned to maximize Trump Accounts, but eligibility requires U.S. citizenship, creating a sharp distinction for H-1B families with foreign-born vs. American-born children.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Hundreds of Masked White Nationalists Marched Through Washington on America's 250th Birthday. They Chanted 'Reclaim America.'
news.excerpt: The Patriot Front's flash-mob march near the US Capitol came hours after Trump called immigrants a 'communist menace' at Mount Rushmore — a jarring backdrop for the 4.8 million Indian Americans celebrating the Fourth of July.
news.image_caption: Patriot Front members march in formation through Washington, D.C.
news.nri_angle: White nationalist group marches through the US capital on July 4, directly challenging the belonging of immigrant communities including the 4.8 million Indian Americans who call America home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Britain Is About to Get Its Seventh Prime Minister in a Decade. The 1.8 Million Indians There Are Watching Closely.
news.excerpt: Andy Burnham is expected to enter Downing Street by July 20 — five days after the India-UK trade deal goes live. His domestic-first agenda could reshape life for Britain's Indian diaspora.
news.image_caption: Andy Burnham, the incoming British Prime Minister, at an event in August 2024
news.nri_angle: Britain's next PM takes over just as the India-UK trade deal goes live, with direct implications for 1.8 million NRIs on social security portability, worker mobility, and the future of India-UK relations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Trump Used America’s 250th Birthday to Call Immigrants a ‘Communist Menace.’ The Diaspora Heard Every Word.
news.excerpt: Speaking beneath Mount Rushmore on the eve of July 4, the president called for ‘newcomers’ who oppose American values to be expelled — language broad enough to alarm four million Indian Americans who built their lives here legally.
news.image_caption: Mount Rushmore in South Dakota, where Trump delivered his July 3 speech on the eve of America's 250th birthday
news.nri_angle: Trump's 'newcomers' rhetoric at Mount Rushmore — calling immigrants a communist menace and vowing to expel them — directly threatens the 4.8 million Indian Americans who built their lives in the US through legal immigration channels.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America's 250th Birthday Was the Hottest on Record. Literally.
news.excerpt: A historic heat dome cancelled parades from Philadelphia to Boston, strained power grids to the breaking point, and forced Trump's Great American State Fair to temporarily shut its gates.
news.image_caption: Crowds gather on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. for Fourth of July celebrations near the Washington Monument
news.nri_angle: Millions of Indian Americans across the East Coast and Mid-Atlantic faced cancelled celebrations and power outages during one of the community's most visible American holiday weekends.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Own Attorney General Called E20 Fuel an 'Experiment.' The Government Spent the Next 48 Hours in Damage Control.
news.excerpt: A viral courtroom video has turned simmering consumer anger over mandatory ethanol-blended petrol into the Modi government's biggest domestic headache this summer.
news.image_caption: A BPCL petrol pump in India, where E20 ethanol-blended fuel is now the only option at nearly all stations
news.nri_angle: NRIs driving in India face the same E20 fuel with no alternative, and the auto sector uncertainty affects diaspora investments in one of India's flagship industries.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and Japan Just Signed Their First Defence Co-Development Deal. It Is the Start of Something Much Bigger.
news.excerpt: Modi and Takaichi summit in New Delhi delivered pacts on AI, stealth naval tech, critical minerals, and a $61 billion investment roadmap — reshaping what the two economies mean to each other.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan during the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit
news.nri_angle: With 1,400 Japanese firms already in India, a 10 trillion yen investment target, and new openings in AI and defence manufacturing, the summit creates direct job and investment pathways for NRI professionals and investors eyeing the India-Japan corridor.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Eight Men Arrested for Stealing Donations From the Ram Mandir. A Court Is Being Asked to Call In the CBI.
news.excerpt: CCTV footage, property raids, and a PIL seeking a CAG audit — the embezzlement scandal at Ayodhya's most sacred site is deepening by the day.
news.image_caption: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya, consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024
news.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs donated to the Ram Mandir construction fund, making this a deeply personal scandal for the diaspora — a PIL in the Allahabad High Court now seeks an independent CAG audit of the Trust's finances.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Turns 250 Tomorrow. No Immigrant Community Has Risen Faster Than Indian Americans.
news.excerpt: As the U.S. marks its semiquincentennial, 5.2 million Indian Americans — now the country's largest Asian ethnic group — are reshaping everything from the C-suite to Capitol Hill. Their story is also getting more complicated.
news.image_caption: July Fourth celebrations at a U.S. Embassy, marking Independence Day
news.nri_angle: Indian Americans are now the largest Asian ethnic group in the US and pay 5-6% of all income taxes despite being 1.5% of the population — the 250th anniversary is as much their celebration as anyone's.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Operation Amistad Wins Hearts in Earthquake-Shattered Venezuela
news.excerpt: Two IAF C-17 Globemasters, 41 medical personnel, and indigenous BHISHM cubes — India's disaster-relief machine reaches Latin America as the death toll crosses 2,600.
news.image_caption: An Indian Air Force aircraft being loaded with humanitarian relief supplies for deployment. India's C-17 Globemasters have become the backbone of its disaster-response operations worldwide.
news.image_credit: Indian Air Force / Government of India (GODL-India), via Wikimedia Commons
news.nri_angle: India's growing first-responder reputation across continents reinforces national pride for the diaspora and underscores New Delhi's expanding strategic engagement with Latin America.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Logged Its Driest June in Fifteen Years. The Next Two Weeks Will Decide What Millions of Farmers Eat.
news.excerpt: Kharif sowing is running 23% behind last year, El Niño is strengthening, and food prices are already climbing. The monsoon's July performance will shape inflation and rural incomes for months to come.
news.image_caption: Parched farmland during a delayed monsoon in India (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: A weak monsoon means higher food bills for families receiving NRI remittances, and potential rice export curbs that would affect diaspora communities in the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Was Personally Invited to Khamenei's Funeral. India Sent a Deputy Minister Instead.
news.excerpt: As Iran stages a week of mass processions for its slain Supreme Leader, India's carefully calibrated delegation reveals the diplomatic tightrope New Delhi walks between Tehran and Washington.
news.image_caption: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an official portrait released during Nowruz celebrations
news.nri_angle: The India-Iran relationship affects Strait of Hormuz negotiations, oil prices, and shipping routes that directly impact NRIs in the Gulf and Indian businesses across the Middle East.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Scrapped Taxes on Its Bonds. $3.4 Billion Poured In Within Weeks.
news.excerpt: New Delhi's most aggressive capital-market reform in years has unlocked record foreign inflows, and Bloomberg's biggest bond index could be next.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata, home to the central bank that broadened bond access for foreign investors
news.nri_angle: NRI investors and the broader diaspora benefit directly from a more accessible, tax-free Indian bond market — and Bloomberg index inclusion would further deepen the pool of rupee-denominated assets available for offshore portfolios.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live in Twelve Days. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora.
news.excerpt: The India-UK CETA eliminates tariffs on 99 percent of Indian exports, opens 137 service sectors, and ends double social security payments for 75,000 professionals. It enters force on July 15.
news.image_caption: UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds and India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal sign the India-UK trade agreement

sources.label: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

news.nri_angle: The Double Contribution Convention ending dual social security payments directly saves Indian professionals in the UK thousands of pounds annually, while 1,800 visas for chefs, yoga instructors, and musicians create new mobility pathways.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Twenty-Six Thousand Indian Australians Signed Up for a Stadium Reception. Then Came the Death Threat.
nri-world.excerpt: The 'Melbourne Meets Modi' reception at Marvel Stadium on July 9 has become the largest Indian diaspora gathering ever planned in Australia — and one of the most contested.
nri-world.image_caption: Marvel Stadium in Melbourne's Docklands, where up to 26,000 Indian Australians are expected on July 9
nri-world.nri_angle: Australia's million-strong Indian-born community navigates competing emotions — rockstar excitement and rising hostility — as it prepares to host Modi in a country still debating how much room to make for its largest overseas-born population.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Melbourne Spent $1.2 Million to Build Australia's First 'Little India.' Not Everyone Is Celebrating.
nri-world.excerpt: Backed by the city's biggest cultural budget in years, the Docklands precinct would join Chinatown and Koreatown as an officially recognised cultural hub — but not without a fight.
nri-world.image_caption: Melbourne's Docklands waterfront, the planned site of Australia's first officially recognised Little India precinct
nri-world.nri_angle: For the quarter-million Indian-born Melburnians who have long lacked a geographic cultural home, the precinct signals institutional acceptance — and reveals the tensions that come with it.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: One Hundred and Thirty Hindu Americans Walked Into Congress on the Fourth of July Eve. Seven Lawmakers Walked Out Allies.
nri-world.excerpt: CoHNA's fifth Hindu Advocacy Day drew bipartisan support from both parties on Capitol Hill, blending the celebration of America's 250th birthday with an urgent pushback against rising Hinduphobia.
nri-world.image_caption: The United States Capitol Building in Washington, D.C., where Hindu American delegates gathered for their fifth annual advocacy day
nri-world.nri_angle: Hindu Americans are building serious political muscle — 130 delegates from 15 states descended on Capitol Hill, held 50-plus meetings with Senate and House staff, visited 120 offices, and secured bipartisan condemnation of temple attacks. This is diaspora civic engagement maturing from protest to policy.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Long Island's India Day Parade Turns Fifteen. The Guest List Now Includes State Senators.
nri-world.excerpt: The curtain raiser for the 15th India Day Parade USA packed 250 people into a government building in Mineola — a far cry from the modest procession that started the tradition in 2011.
nri-world.image_caption: An India Day Parade in the New York metropolitan area — Long Island's edition has grown from a community gathering to a major cultural event (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: What began as a small community parade on Long Island has grown into a celebration so large it draws state senators, county comptrollers, and Indian consular officials — a measure of how deeply Indian Americans have woven themselves into suburban New York's civic fabric.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A New Jersey Temple Has Screened 15,000 People for Free. Now It Wants to Become a Permanent Clinic.
nri-world.excerpt: Health Camp of New Jersey, a volunteer-run nonprofit housed in the Balaji Temple in Bridgewater, is preparing to transform from an annual health fair into a year-round Federally Qualified Health Center.
nri-world.image_caption: A Hindu temple in New Jersey — community health camps at temples have screened over 15,000 people for chronic diseases since 1999 (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian American temples are evolving from spiritual centres into critical community health infrastructure, filling gaps left by the US insurance system for underserved South Asian populations.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: They Read the News from Memory, Without Teleprompters. Now a New York Library Is Making Sure the Diaspora Remembers.
nri-world.excerpt: The Indian Diaspora Center's annual symposium brought Doordarshan veterans and digital-age journalists under one roof in Elmont, New York, to document a media revolution that shaped how millions of Indians — at home and abroad — understood their country.
nri-world.image_caption: Doordarshan Bhavan in New Delhi — a New York symposium is preserving the golden era of Indian television for the diaspora (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: A New York–based diaspora centre is building a permanent archive of Indian community history, using events like this symposium to document the cultural touchstones — Doordarshan chief among them — that connected generations of NRIs to home.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indiaspora Just Catalogued 250 Milestones of Indian American Life. The Timing Is Not a Coincidence.
nri-world.excerpt: Released two days before America's 250th birthday, the compilation spans motel lobbies, yoga studios, Fortune 500 boardrooms — and asks who still gets left out of the story.
nri-world.image_caption: M.R. Rangaswami, founder and chairman of Indiaspora, at a diaspora event
nri-world.nri_angle: A definitive compilation of how Indian Americans have shaped the United States across 15 domains — from hospitality and tech to philanthropy and civil rights — released as America marks its semiquincentennial.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Modi Is Taking His Diaspora Playbook to Three Countries in Six Days. In One of Them, It Will Be Tested.
nri-world.excerpt: A million Indians in Australia, a 40-year gap in New Zealand, and the 'butter chicken tsunami' that won't go away — inside the Indo-Pacific tour that starts Monday.
nri-world.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, whose six-day Indo-Pacific tour begins July 6
nri-world.nri_angle: Modi's three-nation tour includes large-scale diaspora addresses in every stop, but the NZ leg puts a spotlight on rising anti-Indian sentiment and hate crimes that have left the community feeling targeted.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: They Started Fighting for India in Westminster During the Emergency. Fifty Years Later, They Want Blue Plaques.
nri-world.excerpt: FISI UK, the oldest Indian advocacy organisation in Britain, celebrated its golden jubilee with a new initiative to map every Indian trailblazer who lived on British soil.
nri-world.image_caption: The Bhavan Indian Arts Centre in West Kensington, London — venue for the FISI UK Golden Jubilee
nri-world.nri_angle: FISI UK was founded by British Indians in 1976 to give the diaspora a political voice in Westminster. Its 50-year journey mirrors the trajectory of the British Indian community itself — from political invisibility to mainstream influence. The SMRITI initiative now aims to preserve that history for future generations.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Two Duke Cardiologists Now Lead the American Heart Association. Both Are Children of Indian Immigrants.
nri-world.excerpt: Dr. Manesh Patel becomes the first South Asian to serve as AHA volunteer president. His president-elect, Dr. Svati Shah, runs one of the country's leading precision cardiovascular genetics programmes. Both start July 1.
nri-world.image_caption: Duke Chapel on the Duke University campus in Durham, North Carolina — home institution of Dr. Manesh Patel and Dr. Svati Shah, now leading the American Heart Association
nri-world.nri_angle: Two Indian-American doctors simultaneously leading the AHA marks a generational milestone for a community that is overrepresented in medicine but underrepresented in legacy medical leadership. South Asians also face disproportionately high cardiovascular risk, making this appointment personally significant for the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: New Zealand Signed a Trade Deal With India. Then It Quietly Started Writing Immigration Rules That Apply to Indians — and Only Indians.
nri-world.excerpt: Even NZ's own Foreign Minister calls the proposed restrictions discriminatory. Days before Modi's first-ever visit, the country's coalition government is tearing itself apart over who gets to come in.
nri-world.image_caption: New Zealand's Parliament House in Wellington, where the ruling coalition is divided over immigration rules that single out Indian nationals under the newly signed free trade agreement.
nri-world.nri_angle: New Zealand's proposed immigration restrictions specifically target Indian nationals, affecting NRI workers, students, and the 250,000-strong Indian diaspora community — with racist rhetoric and anti-Indian protests compounding the policy threat
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The USISPF Summit Honoured Three Business Titans. Sunil Mittal Used His Speech to Talk About Five Million Indians Instead.
nri-world.excerpt: At the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington, Bharti's chairman and India's ambassador to the US laid out a vision in which the diaspora is not a footnote to the India-US partnership but the load-bearing wall.
nri-world.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman of Bharti Enterprises
nri-world.nri_angle: Mittal explicitly framed the 5-million-strong Indian American community as the strategic bridge between India and the US — in trade, defence, and high technology. Ambassador Kwatra's $30 trillion roadmap positions the diaspora as investors, knowledge partners, and connectors in India's climb to developed-nation status by 2047.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Biggest Healthcare IPO Is Coming — Manipal Health Just Got SEBI's Green Light for a $1.2 Billion Listing
markets-finance.excerpt: The Temasek-backed hospital chain, which runs 48 hospitals and more than 12,000 beds across 14 states, is targeting a late July debut that will test investor appetite for India's booming private healthcare sector.
markets-finance.image_caption: A modern hospital facility in India — Manipal Health operates 48 hospitals with over 12,000 beds across 14 states (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs who use Indian hospitals for medical tourism can now invest in the sector's growth — Manipal's IPO offers exposure to a healthcare boom driven by rising insurance penetration and complex care demand.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits — and SBI's Leveraged Product Promises 11.25%
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI's decision to absorb hedging costs on foreign currency deposits has triggered rate hikes of up to 310 basis points, could draw $35–40 billion in inflows, and is quietly reshaping how Indian banks fund themselves.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee notes — NRI deposit rates have surged after the RBI agreed to absorb currency hedging costs
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn 6-7% on dollar deposits in India — more than US Treasuries — with the RBI absorbing all currency hedging costs through September, creating a rare and time-limited investment window.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Services Engine Just Hit Its Slowest Speed in 17 Months — and Hiring Has Nearly Stalled
markets-finance.excerpt: The HSBC India Services PMI fell sharply to 57.4 in June as domestic demand weakened to its lowest in over two years, even as export orders offered a partial cushion
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors watching the Wall Street GDP upgrades and FPI flow reversal should weigh them against the sharpest services sector deceleration in 17 months — if domestic demand and hiring stay weak, the earnings recovery that fund managers are banking on may not materialise.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: HCLTech Just Landed a $1.14 Billion AI Deal With a European Giant — Its Biggest in Three Years
markets-finance.excerpt: The mega-contract to build an AI-driven digital workplace for a Fortune Global 50 firm is entirely new business, ends a three-year drought in large deals, and lifts the Nifty IT index on a day when global tech is still reeling.
markets-finance.nri_angle: Directly relevant to the tens of thousands of Indian-origin IT professionals and NRI investors with exposure to Indian tech stocks — the deal signals that AI-led transformation is creating new revenue streams, not just destroying old ones.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreign Investors Just Poured a Record $3.4 Billion Into Indian Government Bonds — and a Bloomberg Index Entry Could Unlock Billions More
markets-finance.excerpt: India's decision to scrap taxes on foreign bond investments, combined with falling oil prices and RBI reforms, has triggered the biggest monthly debt inflow on record and put Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index inclusion within reach
markets-finance.image_caption: India's bond market is drawing record foreign investment after sweeping tax reforms
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors can now hold Indian sovereign bonds tax-free after India scrapped withholding and capital gains taxes, making the 6.7% yield one of the most attractive risk-adjusted returns in emerging markets.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: A Weak US Jobs Report Just Took a Fed Rate Hike Off the Table — and India's Markets Are Surging on the News
markets-finance.excerpt: Nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57,000 against expectations of 115,000, sending the dollar to its biggest one-day drop in two months and pushing Indian equities back above the $5 trillion mark for the first time since the Iran crisis began.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — India's equity market has reclaimed the $5 trillion valuation mark
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with US-denominated earnings and India-allocated portfolios benefit directly from a weaker dollar and easing Fed rate fears — the macro backdrop for Indian equities is the most favourable it has been in months.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's IT Giants Face Their Most Scrutinised Earnings Season in Years — and AI Is the Elephant in Every Boardroom
markets-finance.excerpt: With the Nifty IT index down 33% from its February peak, TCS and Infosys are about to report June-quarter results that could determine whether the sector's correction is a buying opportunity or the start of a structural decline.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bangalore — India's IT bellwether reports Q1 FY27 results on July 23
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant IT sector exposure and many work in the very industry under scrutiny — this earnings season is both a portfolio and career signal.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Wall Street Just Raised India's Growth Forecast to 7% — the Sharpest Upward Revision in Over a Year
markets-finance.excerpt: Bank of America, Crisil, and Goldman Sachs have all upgraded India's outlook in the span of a week, citing collapsing oil prices, the Iran peace deal, and a capex surge — while the rupee posts its first quarterly gain since early 2025
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — the central bank's dollar-inflow measures have helped the rupee post its first quarterly gain in over a year
markets-finance.nri_angle: Rupee stability means NRI equity and debt returns are no longer being eroded by currency depreciation; the wave of growth upgrades improves the case for India-linked portfolio allocations.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Bethell's Unbeaten 76 Sinks India at Old Trafford. Bishnoi's 29-Run Over Hands England a 1-0 Series Lead.
sports.excerpt: Arshdeep took two wickets in the first over. Bethell took the match in the 17th. India trail in the five-match T20I series after a four-wicket loss in Manchester.
sports.image_caption: Emirates Old Trafford Cricket Ground in Manchester, venue for the second T20I between England and India
sports.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of NRI fans packed Old Trafford, and millions more watched from the US, Canada, and UK — the T20I series offers the best live cricket viewing opportunity of the British summer.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Ounahi Scores Twice. Morocco End Canada's World Cup on the Fourth of July.
sports.excerpt: Canada were the better team for 45 minutes. Morocco were the better team for the match. A 3-0 loss in Houston ends the co-hosts' best-ever run.
sports.image_caption: Azzedine Ounahi of Morocco during the 2026 FIFA World Cup
sports.nri_angle: Nearly 1.8 million Canadians of Indian origin rallied behind the co-host side — the World Cup gave NRIs in Canada a source of unexpected civic pride, and the run inspired first-time football fans from Brampton to Surrey.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He's 15 Years and 99 Days Old. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Just Broke Sachin Tendulkar's 36-Year Record.
sports.excerpt: The Rajasthan Royals prodigy received his India cap at Old Trafford on Saturday, becoming the youngest male cricketer to represent the country — and ending a debate that began the moment he hit 72 sixes in IPL 2026.
sports.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, India's youngest-ever international cricketer, photographed during a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi
sports.nri_angle: A generational shift in Indian cricket that NRIs across the US, UK, and Canada are watching unfold — the 15-year-old prodigy who broke Sachin's 36-year record represents the IPL era's first truly global cricketing sensation.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Fireworks, Then Football. The World Cup Takes Over the Fourth of July — and NRIs Have the Best Seats in the House.
sports.excerpt: Canada face Morocco in Houston at 1 PM ET. France meet Paraguay in Philadelphia at 5 PM ET. For Indian Americans, a holiday spent watching the world's biggest tournament on American soil is an experience without precedent.
sports.image_caption: The FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 bracket, confirmed after the final Round of 32 matches on July 3
sports.nri_angle: For 4.5 million Indian Americans, the Fourth of July has a new main event — two World Cup knockout matches on American soil, in cities with massive South Asian communities.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Salah Chipped a Panenka. Two Australians Missed. Egypt Made History in Dallas.
sports.excerpt: Mohamed Salah fought through a hamstring strain, scored the nerviest penalty of the shootout, and led Egypt to their first-ever World Cup knockout win — a 4-2 shootout victory over Australia in front of 70,244 fans at AT&T Stadium.
sports.image_caption: Mohamed Salah in action for Egypt's national football team
sports.nri_angle: The match was played at AT&T Stadium in the DFW metroplex — home to one of America's largest NRI communities — while NRIs in Australia saw the Socceroos eliminated from the World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Kohli Is Back. Rohit Is Back. Bumrah Is Back. Gill Will Lead India Into England — and Toward the 2027 World Cup.
sports.excerpt: BCCI announces 15-member ODI squad for three-match series starting July 14 at Edgbaston. Kohli's fitness remains subject to clearance. England name Jofra Archer and uncapped James Coles in their own 16-member squad.

lifestyle-health.title: An Anti-Inflammatory Diet Can Cut Dementia Risk by Nearly a Third — Even After Alzheimer's Has Begun in Your Brain
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 15-year study of nearly 1,900 older adults found that eating foods rich in antioxidants and healthy fats lowered dementia rates by up to 29 percent, even in people whose blood already carried elevated Alzheimer's biomarkers — and the traditional Indian pantry is a natural fit.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Colourful fruits, vegetables, and spices — staples of an anti-inflammatory diet linked to lower dementia risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Traditional Indian diets rich in turmeric, lentils, and spices are naturally anti-inflammatory — but NRIs who shift to processed Western foods may be losing a dietary advantage that could protect against Alzheimer's.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Five Extra Minutes of Sleep and Two Minutes of Exercise a Day Could Add a Full Year to Your Life
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark UK Biobank study of nearly 60,000 adults finds that tiny, simultaneous improvements in sleep, physical activity, and diet compound into as much as 9.4 extra years of disease-free living — and the findings carry outsized implications for South Asians.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh vegetables, whole grains, and fruits — small dietary improvements that compound over time
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated cardiometabolic risk at lower BMI thresholds — this study shows that even tiny concurrent lifestyle changes can yield outsized health gains for diaspora professionals struggling to make time for wellness.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Blood Test Can Now Screen for 10 Cancers — and Zydus and Apollo Are Bringing It to India
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The FDA-designated multi-cancer detection test, built by Guardant Health, uses a simple blood draw to catch bladder, breast, colorectal and seven other cancers before symptoms appear
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A laboratory technician examines blood sample vials for diagnostic testing
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs who schedule health check-ups during visits to India could access a validated multi-cancer blood test through Apollo's nationwide network, and South Asians face distinctive cancer risks that make early multi-cancer screening especially relevant.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Face Elevated Heart Risk by Age 45 Despite Healthier Habits — and the Paradox Runs Deeper Than Diet
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark US study of 2,700 adults finds that South Asian Americans have nearly eight times the prediabetes rate of white peers by midlife — even with better diets and less alcohol. The risk may start at birth.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Cardiovascular screening — new research shows South Asians face elevated heart disease risk by age 45 despite healthier habits (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: Journal of the American Heart Association (Feb. 2026)
South Asian Birth Cohort Study, McMaster University

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Directly impacts the 5.4 million Indian Americans and broader South Asian diaspora — the study reveals they need earlier cardiovascular screening starting in their 40s, not the standard mid-50s guidelines.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Having Weak Muscles and Excess Body Fat Dramatically Raises Your Dementia Risk — and South Asians May Be Uniquely Vulnerable
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark Curtin University study of nearly 500,000 adults finds sarcopenic obesity is a major dementia driver, while being overweight alone is not — if muscle strength is preserved
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult performing resistance training, which new research suggests is critical for protecting brain health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians' well-documented 'skinny fat' phenotype — high visceral fat with low muscle mass — places them at elevated risk for the sarcopenic obesity now linked to dementia, making resistance training an urgent priority for NRI health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Teen's Friends May Shape Their Mental Health More Than You Think — A 600,000-Person Study Shows How
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A massive Finnish study published in JAMA Psychiatry finds that adolescents whose peers have mental health diagnoses are significantly more likely to develop conditions like anxiety and depression themselves — a finding with urgent implications for diaspora families navigating unfamiliar school systems.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Teenagers at school — a 600,000-person Finnish study found peer relationships significantly affect adolescent mental health risk (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRI parents raising teenagers in Western school systems face a peer-influence dynamic that differs sharply from Indian schooling — understanding how their child's social environment shapes mental health risk is essential for early intervention.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Fish Oil Supplements Don't Protect Your Brain From Alzheimer's, a Rigorous Two-Year Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Americans spend over $1 billion a year on fish oil, but a USC clinical trial shows the supplements fail to slow cognitive decline — even though they reach the brain. For South Asians, the findings raise uncomfortable questions about a supplement many families swear by.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fish oil capsules, among the most popular dietary supplements worldwide
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face rising Alzheimer's risk and are heavy fish oil users — this trial suggests they should shift spending from supplements to whole-food diets.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Remote Work Is Making Americans Lonelier and More Depressed — and the Effect Is Worst for Those Who Live Alone
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A sweeping study of 588,000 workers finds that the shift to working from home accounts for a third of the rise in national mental distress since 2011. For Indian-origin tech workers thousands of miles from family, the findings hit close to home.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A remote worker at a home desk — the daily reality for millions in tech and knowledge-economy roles
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers in the US are disproportionately in remotable jobs and far from family — making them especially vulnerable to the isolation the study documents.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Older Adults Who Walk Like Someone 30 Years Younger Have Half the Risk of Cognitive Decline — Even With Alzheimer's Pathology
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark study in Neurology identifies 'super movers' — people over 80 whose brisk gait appears to shield their brains from dementia, offering a deceptively simple biomarker that diaspora families can track as parents age
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult walking briskly through a park — a habit that new research links to sharply lower dementia risk

sources.label: NBC Palm Springs / Univ. of Minnesota

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated diabetes and cardiovascular risk that accelerate cognitive decline; walking speed is a culturally familiar, measurable biomarker diaspora families can track as parents age.

food.title: From a Family Clay Oven to a James Beard Nod: The Immigrant Story Behind Las Vegas's Hottest Indian Restaurant
food.excerpt: Tamba — named for the Hindi word for copper — earned a Best New Restaurant finalist nod from the James Beard Foundation in its first year, capping a three-decade journey that began with an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant.
food.image_caption: A traditional tandoor clay oven, the centrepiece of Indian cooking that gave the Dhillon family's first restaurant its name
food.nri_angle: Tamba's journey from an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant to a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist mirrors the larger arc of Indian cuisine's ascent in America, offering diaspora families a powerful narrative of generational ambition rewarded.

carousel.title: Indian-Made Gasoline Is Reaching Russia Through Traders. New Delhi Says It Has Nothing to Do With It.
carousel.excerpt: As Ukrainian drone strikes cripple a third of Russia's refining capacity, fuel from Nayara Energy — 49% owned by Rosneft — is sailing north via intermediaries. India's oil minister insists no Indian company is selling directly. The distinction may not hold for long.
carousel.nri_angle: India-Russia fuel trade complicates the India-US trade deal that directly affects five million Indian Americans and Indian exporters.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Twenty-One ₹100-Crore Films. One Man. Akshay Kumar Just Rewrote Bollywood History.
carousel.excerpt: Welcome to the Jungle crossed ₹100 crore in nine days, giving Akshay Kumar a record no other Indian actor is even close to touching — and the franchise that started 19 years ago just proved it's indestructible.
carousel.image_caption: Akshay Kumar, whose Welcome to the Jungle just became his 21st ₹100-crore film (Wikimedia Commons)
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Bethell's Unbeaten 76 Sinks India at Old Trafford. Bishnoi's 29-Run Over Hands England a 1-0 Series Lead.
carousel.excerpt: Arshdeep took two wickets in the first over. Bethell took the match in the 17th. India trail in the five-match T20I series after a four-wicket loss in Manchester.
carousel.image_caption: Emirates Old Trafford Cricket Ground in Manchester, venue for the second T20I between England and India
carousel.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of NRI fans packed Old Trafford, and millions more watched from the US, Canada, and UK — the T20I series offers the best live cricket viewing opportunity of the British summer.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India's First Private Orbital Rocket Is Ready to Fly. The Launch Window Opens in a Week.
carousel.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 — seven stories tall, carbon composite, 3D-printed engines — will attempt to reach orbit from Sriharikota as early as July 12. A $1 billion valuation says the market believes it can.
carousel.image_caption: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota, India's first private space launch in 2022
carousel.nri_angle: For Indian aerospace engineers at SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Boeing, Skyroot represents a credible private space company in India — a career path and investment opportunity that did not exist five years ago.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India's Biggest Healthcare IPO Is Coming — Manipal Health Just Got SEBI's Green Light for a $1.2 Billion Listing
carousel.excerpt: The Temasek-backed hospital chain, which runs 48 hospitals and more than 12,000 beds across 14 states, is targeting a late July debut that will test investor appetite for India's booming private healthcare sector.
carousel.image_caption: A modern hospital facility in India — Manipal Health operates 48 hospitals with over 12,000 beds across 14 states (Wikimedia Commons)
carousel.nri_angle: NRIs who use Indian hospitals for medical tourism can now invest in the sector's growth — Manipal's IPO offers exposure to a healthcare boom driven by rising insurance penetration and complex care demand.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk
